'''Alevtina Pavlovna Shmeleva''' ({{langx|ru|Алевтина Павловна Шмелева}}; 11 June 1928 – 25 April 2022) was a Russian nuclear physicist.

She studied at the [[Moscow State Linguistic University|Moscow Institute of Foreign Languages]] for two years, before she found her dedication within physics and particle detectors at the [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|Moscow Engineering and Physics University]], where she graduated in 1954. Shmeleva joined the Elementary Particles Laboratory in the [[Lebedev Physical Institute|P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (LPI)]] under the guidance of academician [[Artem Alikhanian|Artyom Alikhanian]]. He was the scientific adviser of PhD thesis of Aleftina Shmeleva.<ref name="DisserShmeleva">Shmeleva Alevtina Pavlovna, Atomic number dependence of the inelastic cross-sections of neutrons and pions at the energy of 100 GeV, PhD thesis ([[Candidate of Sciences]] in Physics and Mathematics), doctoral adviser professor [[Artem Alikhanian|Artyom Alikhanian]], Moscow, 1969, 140 pages, BBK-code В385.22, В382.232, specialty 01.00.00: Physics and mathematics, in Russian, stored in [https://www.rsl.ru/en Russian State Library], index OD Дк 69-1/1282</ref>
The first job after graduating from the institute in 1954 was participation in expeditions to the [[Mount Aragats]] [[Aragats Cosmic Ray Research Station|cosmic ray research station]] and later to the Nor Amberd station in [[Armenia]]. Here, studies of cosmic rays were carried out at the heights of mountains with the help of magnetic spectrometers. Shmeleva led the work on the creation of a spark calorimeter for these experiments. These studies measured intensity and composition of the nuclear component of cosmic rays at altitude 2000 meters above sea level in the energy range 100-300 GeV.<ref name="LabElemPart">[http://npad.lebedev.ru/docs/istlabnew3.pdf "Laboratory of Elementary Particles. (Past. Present. Future.)", editor G. I. Merzon, (in russian), published by FIAN, Moscow, 2012.]</ref> Later she started to work with [[Transition radiation detector|Transition Radiation Detector]] prototypes, which were rather new at this time and which required pioneering skills.

Between 1976 and 1988, Shmeleva participated in the development of a full absorption spectrometer on liquid xenon with a volume of 40 liters. The created spectrometer had the best energy resolution for that time of 3.5% <math>/ \sqrt{E(GeV)} </math> and coordinate resolution of 5.6&nbsp;mm<math>/ \sqrt{E(GeV)} </math>.<ref name="LabElemPart" />

From 1980 to 1988 she participated in the R808 experiment to study the production of prompt photons at the world's first proton collider ISR at CERN. For this experiment, employees of the Lebedev Physical Institute, INR, MEPhI and INP SB RAS developed hodoscope panels for shower counters based on scintillator NaI(Tl) crystals with a total weight of about one ton.<ref name="LabElemPart" />

In 1977 Shmeleva and her husband {{ill|Boris Dolgoshein|ru|Долгошеин, Борис Анатольевич}} from [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|MEPhI]] participated in the International Symposium on Transition Radiation<ref name="SymposiumErevan">{{cite web|url=https://inis.iaea.org/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/10/466/10466998.pdf|title=Proceedings of International Symposium on Transition Radiation of High Energy Particles, Yerevan, 12–17 May 1977}}</ref> in [[Erevan]], [[Armenia]], where they met [[William J. Willis]], whom they managed to convince about the concept of cluster-counting [[Transition radiation detector|Transition Radiation Detectors (TRDs)]], and he invited the LPI-MEPhI group to [[CERN]]
<ref name="ArtemAlikhanian">{{Cite web |url=http://www.rfbr.ru/rffi/ru/books/o_36159 |title=B. A. Dolgoshein, A. P. Shmeleva, Twenty years later, page 181 in A. Alikhanian: Essays, Recollections, Documents (mainly in Russian), edited by G. Merzon, Moscow, 2000, 335 p. (Артем Алиханян. Очерки, воспоминания, документы) |access-date=2022-05-24 |archive-date=2022-04-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406123716/https://www.rfbr.ru/rffi/ru/books/o_36159 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
to realise the idea. Since then, Shmeleva collaborated with the particle physics community at [[CERN]]. From 1978 to 1988, she coordinated the work of the Lebedev group, building prototype TRDs, testing them at the [[Super Proton Synchrotron|SPS]] and delivering the TRD of the HELIOS experiment at the [[Super Proton Synchrotron|SPS]] ([[List of Super Proton Synchrotron experiments|NA34/1 and NA34/2]]).<ref name="LabElemPart" />
As an expert in [[transition radiation detector]]s, Shmeleva joined the challenging [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] TRT project at [[Large Hadron Collider]], where she and the Lebedev group<ref name="InterviewFIAN">{{cite web|url=http://www.fian-inform.ru/intervyu/item/523-fian-i-tsern|title=Alevtina Shmeleva and collaboration of FIAN with CERN|publisher=// Site [[Lebedev Physical Institute|P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute (LPI)]]|accessdate=2022-05-11}}</ref> started in the very early days of RD6, the preparations of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] TRT. Shmeleva and her team,<ref name="LHCStart">{{cite web|url=https://www.nanonewsnet.ru/articles/2009/eksklyuzivnye-podrobnosti-probnogo-zapuska-bolshogo-adronnogo-kollaidera|title=Alevtina Shmeleva as the team leader of FIAN group of ATLAS TRT at LHC at CERN}}</ref> since then, were pillars of the TRT collaboration.

Shmeleva was sensitive to the medical outreach of the fundamental science research, in particular with Vadim Kantzerov ([[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute)|MEPhI]]) she developed medical gamma locator.<ref name="Locator">{{cite web|url=https://poisknews.ru/magazine/6171/|title=Contribution of Alevtina Shmeleva to the medical gamma locator}}</ref>
 
Shmeleva had strong linguistic background and physics knowledge. She communicated well with colleagues.<ref name="PhDMashinistov">{{cite web|url=http://old.lebedev.ru/direct/show_file.php?tname=dissertation&id_tname=154|title=Aleftina Shmeleva as PHD adviser of R.Mashinistov}}</ref><ref name="Muraviev">{{cite web|url=https://atlas-service-enews.web.cern.ch/2009/news_09/news_mouraviev.php|title=Article of A. Shmeleva on her collaborator Sergey Muraviev}}</ref> She brought people together and ensured that problems were solved.
